title: The conormal module of a relative global complete intersection is free on the equations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$ integers and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that $S=P/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Let $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)\subseteq P$; the conormal module $I/I^2$ is an $S=P/I$-module. Then $I/I^2$ is a free $S$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with basis the classes $f_1\bmod I^2,\dots,f_c\bmod I^2$; in particular $I/I^2\cong S^{\oplus c}$.

proof.text: Write I=span(range f), S=P/I and e_j the image of f_j in I/I². For an element of I, ideal-span induction expresses its conormal class in the span of the e_j over P: generators, zero, sums and scalar multiples are handled by linearity of toCotangent. Surjectivity of P→S and restrictScalars_span then give span_S(e_j)=I/I². This is the proved private helper span_conormal_generators.

For any prime m of P containing I, q=m.map(P→P/I) is prime and q.comap(P→P/I)=m by the quotient ideal correspondence. Apply isRegular_localization_of_relativeGlobalCompleteIntersection to q, and transport along this equality, to obtain regularity of the image of f in P_m. The dependent prime proof is transported by equality induction, not by a new assumption.

Suppose ∑ a_j f_j lies in I². At a maximal ideal m containing I, put B=P_m and g_j=f_j/1. Ideal.map_span identifies I B with span(range g), and Ideal.map_pow maps the relation into (I B)². By regularSequence_conormal_free the g_j classes form a basis. The class of the mapped relation is ∑ (a_j/1 mod I B) times the j-th basis vector and is zero. Linear independence gives a_j/1∈I B for every j. The calculation is proved in conormal_sum and coefficients_mem_of_conormal_basis, and combined in coefficients_mem_of_locally_regular.

At a maximal ideal m not containing I, Ideal.map(I) in P_m is the unit ideal: take t∈I outside m, whose image is a unit. Therefore every a_j/1 is in I B at every maximal ideal. Apply Ideal.mem_of_localization_maximal to each a_j to obtain a_j∈I. This is the final part of the proved helper coefficients_mem_of_locally_regular.

For a relation ∑ s_j e_j=0 over S, choose lifts a_j∈P using the proved quotient surjectivity. By conormal_sum and toCotangent_eq_zero its lifted combination lies in I². Steps 2–4 give a_j∈I and hence s_j=0. Fintype.linearIndependent_iff gives linear independence of e. Module.Basis.mk combines this with step 1; mk_apply gives the prescribed equation classes. Module.Free.of_basis and b.equivFun give freeness and the requested isomorphism to Fin c→S. All constructions and calculations also hold when c=0 or S=0.
